name: Skew Expiry Credit
description: Expiry credit spreads that sell the relatively rich side of the 100-point NIFTY IV skew (spot-based Black-Scholes IV, session-local EMA-10, 800-minute rank), hedged 400 points away; put spreads only while the 20-session realised volatility is at most 16%; the 50% credit target applies on the entry day only, then the position runs to the 14:57 expiry-day exit or the stop.
summary: Weekly-expiry NIFTY credit spreads that sell whichever side of the options market is relatively expensive.
exit_policy: 50% of entry credit target on the entry day only, 5% margin stop, 14:57 exit on expiry day
limitations: Gross historical simulation on Dhan minute closes, 26 Jan 2022 to 19 Nov 2026, the earliest start Dhan's five years of data allow once the volatility rule has its history; missing option quotes, estimated margin and excluded costs make results provisional. The gate and put filter were tuned on Oct 2025 to Sep 2026, so everything before Oct 2025 is out of sample: 72 trades, 49% winners, 37 stops, INR 4.56 lakh, against 16 trades, 16 winners, no stops and INR 4.85 lakh in the fitted year. The results depend on fill timing: this replay fills at the close of the signal candle, and the strategy re-enters straight after a stop, where a minute changes the outcome. With every fill one candle later and real costs the same history gives INR 6.77 lakh and a 36.1% drawdown (INR 5.68 lakh and 31.6% from 4 Oct 2023); on that basis same-day trades lose money overall, and on 26 Jan 2022 to 3 Oct 2023 it beat only 84% of random-entry runs. Skew Afternoon Credit trades the same signal from 11:45 with a stop that waits an hour and is far less sensitive to this. The -22.9% maximum drawdown is four put-spread stops on 4 June 2024. All four listed strategies show this full history, so their figures are comparable.
rules: Nearest weekly NIFTY expiry; entries 10:15-14:15 IST, never on expiry day, at most five days to expiry.
Skew = own Black-Scholes IV of the 100-point OTM put minus the 100-point OTM call (spot underlying, 6.5% rate), smoothed with a session-local exponential mean of span 10.

Credit CALL spread when the smoothed skew <= -3.0 IV points and its 800-minute rank is below 0.2; credit PUT spread when it is >= 4.5, the rank is above 0.8 and the annualised realised volatility of the last 20 daily index returns is at most 16%. No entries in weekend special sessions.
Sell the ATM strike of the last completed candle's open; buy 400 points further OTM; same expiry.
Target: spread value at 50% of entry credit, on the entry day only. Stop: entry credit plus 5% of normal margin per lot. Scheduled exit 14:57 IST on expiry day.
Sizing: floor(allocation / estimated margin); 80% of capital on Mondays from 6 April 2026, else 100%.
One position at a time; one evaluation per completed minute; no same-minute re-entry.

name: Skew Afternoon Credit
description: The Skew Expiry Credit signal traded only in the afternoon, with a stop that waits an hour: expiry credit spreads on the rich side of the 100-point NIFTY IV skew, hedged 400 points away, entered from 11:45, with a 40% entry-day credit target and a credit + 50 stop active from 60 minutes after entry (a credit + 100 disaster stop is always on).
summary: The IV-skew signal traded in the afternoon session only, with a more patient stop.
exit_policy: 40% of entry credit target on the entry day only; stop at credit + 50 from 60 minutes after entry, credit + 100 at any time; 14:57 exit on expiry day
limitations: Gross historical simulation on Dhan minute closes, 26 Jan 2022 to 19 Nov 2026, the earliest start Dhan's five years of data allow once the volatility rule has its history; missing option quotes, estimated margin and excluded costs make results provisional. The signal is Skew Expiry Credit's (fitted on Oct 2025 to Sep 2026); the entry start, stop, grace period and target were chosen on 4 Oct 2023 to 30 Sep 2026 from about 1,500 variants. Every rule was chosen on data from 4 Oct 2023 onward, so that part of this backtest (55 trades, INR 10.49 lakh) is in sample; only 26 Jan 2022 to 3 Oct 2023 (16 trades, INR 0.92 lakh) was never used by a search. With next-candle fills and real costs those 16 trades made INR 83,992 and beat only 78% of random-entry runs, so the evidence of an edge outside the searched years is weak; on that basis the whole history gives INR 10.43 lakh and a 21.2% drawdown. The drawdown is sensitive to fill timing: from 4 Oct 2023 it is 10.1% here but 20.8% when every fill is one candle later, because one trade on 23 Oct 2026 then misses its target by half a point and is stopped. Lots are sized on margin alone: a spread that opens beyond its stop after an overnight gap can lose about a quarter of capital in one trade, and four of the six stops in the early period were gap opens. The -19.5% maximum drawdown is three call-spread stops on 22-30 March 2022. All four listed strategies show this full history, so their figures are comparable.

Sell the ATM strike of the last completed candle's open; buy 400 points further OTM; same expiry.

Target: spread value at 60% of entry credit (40% of the credit captured), on the entry day only. Stop: entry credit plus 50 points (5.56% of normal margin per lot), checked from 60 minutes after entry; a disaster stop at credit plus 100 applies from entry. Scheduled exit 14:57 IST on expiry day.

name: Momentum Geometric Capped
description: Momentum Geometric signal with drawdown-capped risk: a tighter stop, a 2.5% loss cap per trade and a one-session pause after every stop.
summary: The Momentum Geometric signal with tighter, drawdown-capped risk per trade.
exit_policy: 10-point spread target; stop at credit + 35; one-session pause after a stop
limitations: Gross 3-year historical simulation (4 Oct 2023 - 19 Nov 2026, fixed INR 320,000). The signal formula was chosen on Jul 2025 - Oct 2026 data and these risk rules on all three years, so results are in-sample; drawdown is sensitive to the trade sequence (a two-session pause is much worse). Missing option quotes, estimated margin and excluded costs make results provisional; it trades about 110-140 times a year, so costs matter. 1 Oct to 19 Nov 2026 was added on 20 Nov 2026 with no rule changed: 12 trades, -INR 59,566; the maximum drawdown went from -16.8% to -24.3%. One position entered on 19 Nov 2026 was still open at the end of the data and is not counted. Taken off the mainboard on 24 Nov 2026 after its reliability check: it passed 5 of 11 rules set beforehand. With next-candle fills, real costs and exits on schedule, 26 Jan 2022 to 19 Nov 2026 gave INR 3.56 lakh, 16.8% a year, with a 56.4% drawdown in the first half of 2022; costs took more than half of the profit and doubled costs turn it into a loss. On 26 Jan 2022 to 3 Oct 2023, which no search used, it made INR 0.44 lakh and beat only 72% of random-entry runs. Overnight gap stops broke the 2.5% loss cap, the worst losing 12.3% of capital in one trade.

name: Skew Deep Credit
description: Skew Afternoon Credit with a deeper short strike, the one change kept from a 1,005-variant search: the short strike sits 50 points in the money for a larger credit. Entries from 11:45, 400-point hedge, 40% entry-day credit target, credit + 50 stop active from 60 minutes after entry (credit + 100 disaster stop always on). Put spreads are blocked when realised volatility is above 16%, as in Skew Afternoon Credit; this strategy was first listed without that block and it was restored on 22 Nov 2026.
summary: Skew Afternoon Credit tuned for a larger credit per trade.
exit_policy: 40% of entry credit target on the entry day only; stop at credit + 50 from 60 minutes after entry, credit + 100 at any time; 14:57 exit on expiry day
limitations: Gross historical simulation on Dhan minute closes, 26 Jan 2022 to 19 Nov 2026, the earliest start Dhan's five years of data allow once the volatility rule has its history; missing option quotes, estimated margin and excluded costs make results provisional. The signal is Skew Expiry Credit's (fitted on Oct 2025 to Sep 2026) and the execution is Skew Afternoon Credit's; the in-the-money short strike was the best of 1,005 further variants tried on 4 Oct 2023 to 30 Sep 2026 (about 2,500 with the earlier search). Every rule was chosen on data from 4 Oct 2023 onward, so that part of this backtest (56 trades, INR 11.28 lakh) is in sample; only 26 Jan 2022 to 3 Oct 2023 (18 trades, INR 1.36 lakh) was never used by a search. With next-candle fills and real costs those 18 trades made INR 98,166 and beat only 80% of random-entry runs, so the evidence of an edge outside the searched years is weak. Until 22 Nov 2026 this strategy also sold put spreads at any realised volatility; over this history that version had a 42.7% drawdown after costs against 23.0%, so the volatility block was restored before any paper trade. Lots are sized on margin alone: a spread that opens beyond its stop after an overnight gap can lose about a quarter of capital in one trade, and five of the 18 early trades were gap stops. The -21.7% maximum drawdown is three call-spread stops on 22-30 March 2022; four call-spread stops in a row on 23-27 Oct 2026 cost 19.2%. All four listed strategies show this full history, so their figures are comparable.

name: Momentum Afternoon Credit
description: Overnight NIFTY credit spreads from plain price momentum: the 45-minute index move is ranked against the last 800 minutes, and a strong rise sells a put spread while a strong fall sells a call spread. Entries from 11:45 only, 400-point hedge, credit + 45 stop, no profit target, exit the next session, and lots capped so one stop loses at most 2.5% of capital. It uses no option-volume term, unlike the other momentum strategies.
summary: Overnight NIFTY credit spreads that follow strong late-morning price momentum, with a capped loss per trade.
exit_policy: No profit target; stop at credit + 45; next-session exit capped at expiry; lots capped at a 2.5% loss per stop
limitations: Gross historical simulation on Dhan minute closes, 26 Jan 2022 to 19 Nov 2026, fixed INR 320,000; missing option quotes, estimated margin and excluded costs make results provisional. It is the best of about 2,500 variants searched on 4 Oct 2023 to 19 Nov 2026, so that part of this backtest (427 trades, INR 7.76 lakh) is in sample, and luck alone gives a best variant that good about one time in fifteen; only 26 Jan 2022 to 3 Oct 2023 (238 trades, INR 2.97 lakh) was never used by a search. The data has no price for the 400-point hedge once the index has moved about 100 points in the trade's favour. The 149 exits it affects close on schedule here, with the hedge valued by an option-pricing model from its last traded price (2.72 points on average) rather than a quote. With every fill one candle later and real costs (about INR 434 a trade), 14 Dec 2021 to 19 Nov 2026 gives INR 5.88 lakh, 23.6% a year and a 26.8% drawdown, past the 25% listing limit; the part before 4 Oct 2023 gives 21.2% a year and beat 92% of random-entry runs, short of the 95% rule. On that basis it passed 6 of 11 reliability rules set beforehand: doubled costs take the drawdown to 34.8%, a 640-minute rank or an 11:15 start halves the profit, and 19 of 22 setting changes of about 20% push the drawdown past 25%. The 2.5% loss cap does not hold when a spread opens beyond its stop after an overnight gap: 42 such stops cost INR 4.76 lakh on that basis and the worst lost 8.4% of capital in one trade. The -20.1% maximum drawdown is 14 stops in 25 trades between 30 Oct 2023 and 3 Jan 2024. One position entered on 19 Nov 2026 was still open at the end of the data and is not counted. All four listed strategies show this full history, so their figures are comparable.

rules.label: Price momentum
rules.description: 45-minute price change (close against the open 45 candles earlier), ranked over 800 observed candles. No option volume or option volatility is used.

rules.label: Bullish
rules.description: Rank > 0.9: sell ATM put, buy put 400 points lower.

rules.label: Bearish
rules.description: Rank < 0.1: sell ATM call, buy call 400 points higher.

rules.label: Entry window
rules.description: 11:45–14:15 IST. ATM from the last completed candle's open. Positive spread credit; short premium ≤200.

rules.label: Risk & holding
rules.description: Stop at entry credit + 45 points (5% of estimated margin). No profit target. Next-session exit (14:53), capped at expiry.

rules.label: Sizing
rules.description: Lots from estimated margin, then capped so one stop loses at most 2.5% of capital (about 3 lots); 80% of capital on Mondays.

rules.label: Position
rules.description: One position at a time; one evaluation per completed minute; no same-minute re-entry.

name: Momentum Expiry Puts
description: Buys one at-the-money NIFTY put on expiry day or the day before (and the Friday before) when the index has fallen for three hours, the last five minutes have not extended the fall, at-the-money option volatility is at the top of its last 375 minutes and puts are no dearer than calls. About 7.5% of capital goes into premium; the option is sold at 80% of its price (stop), at three times its price (target) or at 15:10. At most two trades a day.
summary: Buys a near-expiry NIFTY put after a three-hour fall; small cut losses, rare large wins, same-day exit.
exit_policy: Stop at 80% of the premium paid; target at 300% (+200%); otherwise out at 15:10 the same day
limitations: Historical simulation on Dhan minute closes, 26 Jan 2022 to 19 Nov 2026, fixed INR 320,000, 7.5% of it in premium per trade; fills one candle after the signal with 1% slippage each way, before brokerage and taxes (after them the five years make about INR 5.63 lakh instead of 5.84 lakh, drawdown 20.7%). The trade rules began as those of a marketplace option-buying algo, whose entry rule could not be recovered; the entry rule here is the best of 5,000 searched on 1 Dec 2025 to 19 Nov 2026, and the stop, target and size were then chosen from 721 variants ranked on 2022-2024 only. On 1 Jan 2025 to 19 Nov 2026, which that ranking never used, it made 23% a year after costs with a 17% drawdown. It wins about one trade in five: most trades are small cut losses and the profit comes from a few large winners, so runs of ten or more losing trades are normal. It has not been through the full reliability checklist. Option buying near expiry loses the premium quickly when the index stops moving.

rules.label: Trend
rules.description: NIFTY down at least 0.10% over the last 180 one-minute candles.

rules.label: Pause
rules.description: The last 5 minutes have not fallen more than 0.05%: the fall has stalled for now.

rules.label: Volatility
rules.description: At-the-money implied volatility (call and put averaged) ranks in the top 5% of its last 375 minutes.

rules.label: Option pricing
rules.description: The at-the-money put's implied volatility is no higher than the call's.

rules.label: Days and hours
rules.description: Expiry day, the day before, or the Friday before a Tuesday expiry; entries 09:45-13:35; at most two trades a day.

rules.label: Size
rules.description: Lots = 7.5% of capital / (put price x lot size), rounded down.

rules.label: Exits
rules.description: Sell at 80% of the price paid (stop), at three times it (target), or at 15:10.
